{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development and Hosting Agreement, HDI / Company)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Subject:** Playbook review findings and negotiation posture

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified **19 findings**: 2 critical, 6 high, 8 medium and 2 low, of which **5 are compliant** and require no action. The Agreement is materially incomplete in our favour on risk allocation and unusually restrictive on our commercial freedom.

The two critical gaps are structural: the Agreement contains **no intellectual property or data ownership provision anywhere** — HDI builds and hosts the Site using our Content, yet nothing allocates ownership of the deliverables or of our Content, customer and user data — and **no limitation of liability, exclusion of damages or aggregate cap at all**, leaving both parties fully exposed at law. We have inserted a new Section 5.5 (ownership and embedded-IP licence) and a new Section 10.9 (mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs at the fallback level).

The high-severity issues cluster around exit and exclusivity. Section 6.1 imposes **full-term exclusive dealing** on us across Deerskin Products and "substantially similar" products, and hands HDI the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site, with no performance-based exit and a term that auto-renews annually — walk-away territory, addressed at the preferred position under both the exclusivity and non-compete rules. Section 4.2(a) imposes a **Termination Payment untethered to fees** (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000) while Section 4.1 gives us **no convenience exit at all** during a term; we have added a Company convenience right on 90 days' notice and capped the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees. Section 1.4's inbound use rights do not extend to our affiliates or survive an M&A transfer, and Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause that neither protects our assignment rights nor gates HDI's.

At the medium and low levels we have added HDI insurance, a performance warranty, an HDI IP indemnity, post-termination transition and data export, an exclusive New York forum, a once-per-year cap on HDI's inspection right, and shortened the non-renewal notice window from 90 to 60 days. Five items — MFN, minimum commitments and non-solicitation among them — already sit at our preferred position and are not redlined.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Agreement-wide (no provision); insert new § 5.5 |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability, mutuality and carve-outs | Missing | Agreement-wide (no provision); insert new § 10.9 |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (carve-out § 6.2; HDI covenant § 6.3 retained) |
| 4 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 4.2(a); new § 4.2(d) cap |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | §§ 4.1, 4.2(a) |
| 7 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10.3 |
| 8 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 |
| 9 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Agreement-wide (no provision); insert new § 10.9 |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Missing | § 9 (authority reps only); insert § 9(c) |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 4 (no exit mechanic); insert new § 4.3 |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § 4.1 |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | §§ 1.8, 3.1 (no Customer MFN) |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | §§ 3.1–3.3 (usage-based only) |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 (liaison only; no covenant) |
| 17 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 10.5 (NY law retained; forum added) |
| 18 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 9 / § 10 (no indemnity); insert § 9(c) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions our playbook treats as walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on each.

1. **Full-term exclusive dealing and brand exclusivity (§ 6.1)** — the restriction runs for the whole term, which auto-renews annually under § 4.1, exceeding the 12-month fallback ceiling, and there is no automatic exit for HDI's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates (§ 1.6 gives only a one-off launch-delay right, and terminating otherwise triggers the § 4.2 Termination Payment). The narrow § 6.2 closeout carve-out does not cure this. HDI's exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand independently blocks us from using and licensing our brand. Redlined to non-exclusivity; HDI's own § 6.3 restrictions, which benefit us, are untouched.
2. **No Vendor indemnity of any kind (§§ 9, 10)** — HDI designs, hosts and operates the Site but gives us no protection against third-party IP infringement claims. Cured at the fallback: new § 9(c) with the three customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3× twelve-month-fee super-cap.
3. **No insurance obligation anywhere** — HDI hosts the Site and, under § 8.1, has access to our Content, user information and data. Inserted at the preferred level in new § 10.9 (CGL $1M/$2M, E&O $2M, cyber and privacy $5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O $1M / cyber $2M) available in negotiation.
4. **Unlimited HDI inspection right (§ 3.4)** — no frequency limit, edging toward the walk-away position on unlimited audits. Single minimal edit adds a once-per-twelve-month cap; the favourable 30-day notice, business-hours and HDI-borne-cost terms are retained verbatim.

We also flag, as closely adjacent risk, the combination of **no liability cap at all** with an **uncapped, fee-untethered Termination Payment** and **no convenience exit** — individually addressed above, but together they leave us with unbounded downside and no clean way out.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Circulate the redline** with the four inserted provisions (§ 5.5 ownership, § 10.9 liability cap, § 10.9 insurance, § 4.3 transition) and the § 6.1 replacement flagged as our priority asks.
2. **Lead with the walk-away set** — § 6.1 exclusivity/brand rights, HDI indemnity, insurance and the audit frequency cap. Signal that exclusivity and indemnity are threshold issues, not trades.
3. **Negotiate the exit package as a unit** — the new Company convenience right on 90 days' notice, the § 4.2(d) three-month cap on the Termination Payment, and the § 4.1 non-renewal window at 60 days. We have deliberately not pressed the preferred 30-day/pro-rata-refund package, which would require reworking the whole Section 4 bargain; that remains available as a later concession only if the cap holds.
4. **Confirm the drafting mechanics on the three repaired items** (LD § 4.2(d), T4C, INDEMN § 9(c)) before issuing: the § 4.2(a) computation is retained verbatim so the § 4.2(b) zero-value determination and § 4.2(c) instalment mechanic still operate, and the inserted indemnity carries its own "(c)" designation so the super-cap's internal cross-reference resolves against retained §§ 9(a)–(b).
5. **Hold the fallback trades in reserve**: insurance at E&O $1M / cyber $2M; transition preferred extras (six months at then-current rates, machine-readable export, certified deletion); the RENEWAL 30-day opt-out and Vendor reminder; and the preferred LOL floor, consequential-damages exclusion and wider carve-out set, which we have not volunteered.
6. **No action** on MFN, MINCOMMIT and NOSOLICIT — each sits at our preferred position. Retain § 1.8 (HDI to promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favourably than its own catalog titles) and § 6.3 unchanged; both run in our favour.
"}
